---
name: "spec-design-validator"
description: "Use this agent when you need a specification, technical design document, or implementation plan pressure-tested with brutal honesty before engineering work begins. This agent hunts for architectural flaws, unstated assumptions, missing requirements, over-engineering, scope creep, integration risks, and delivers clear go/no-go/revise guidance.

<example>
Context: A developer has drafted a technical design document for a new caching-strategy module and wants it validated before implementation begins.
user: "I've finished the technical design doc for the new multi-region request router. Can you validate it before we start building?"
assistant: "I'm going to use the Agent tool to launch the spec-design-validator agent to pressure-test the design document for architectural flaws, missing requirements, and implementation risks."
<commentary>
Since the user has completed a technical design and wants validation before implementation, use the spec-design-validator agent to perform brutal review of the spec.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: A team lead has drafted an implementation plan for a GitHub issue and wants it validated before assigning to engineers.
user: "Here's my implementation plan for issue #42 — the new MCP server for a third-party payments integration. Plan covers 5 phases over 3 weeks."
assistant: "Let me use the Agent tool to launch the spec-design-validator agent to pressure-test this implementation plan before we commit engineering resources."
<commentary>
The user has produced an implementation plan and needs it validated for scope, sequencing, risk, and feasibility before delegating work.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: A test engineer has written a test plan and spec for a new feature.
user: "I've drafted the test plan and spec for the job queue feature. Ready for review?"
assistant: "I'll use the Agent tool to launch the spec-design-validator agent to rigorously validate the spec and test plan for completeness, edge cases, and hidden assumptions."
<commentary>
The user has produced a spec/test plan that needs validation before implementation — exactly the spec-design-validator's domain.
</commentary>
</example>"
model: opus
color: red
---
